10.title: THE MIRROR
paragraphs: “So because I did it once, you’ve been doing it for years?”
“I continued because having the money made me feel safe.”
Your spouse looks directly at you.
That may be the most honest thing said all evening.

11.title: ONE QUESTION
paragraphs: Before the conversation ends, your spouse asks:
“If I had told you about the account when it had $5,000 in it, what would you have wanted us to do with the money?”

13.title: WHAT HAPPENS NOW
paragraphs: Neither of you has checked the clock for a while.
The dishes are still on the table.
The bank statement lies between you.

01.title: TITLE
paragraphs: The difficult part is knowing which is which.

02.title: THE DRAWER
paragraphs: You pull a bank statement from the bedroom drawer just as the front door opens. You were looking for your passport.
The statement is for a US-dollar savings account at a Kampala bank. It belongs to your spouse. You have never heard of it.
Eleven years married. Six months ago, when the washing machine died, your spouse said, “We really need to be careful. We don’t have spare money.”
Your spouse calls from the hallway: “Found it?”
The statement is still in your hand.

03a.title: THE TABLE
paragraphs: Your spouse walks into the kitchen.
“Why were you going through my things?”
There is $47,263 sitting between you, and somehow you are the one being questioned.

03b.title: THE PHOTOGRAPH
paragraphs: Put it back exactly where you found it.
Someone laughs at something on television.
At 1:17 a.m., you are still awake.
Your spouse is asleep beside you.
Their phone is on the bedside table.

03b2.title: THE PHONE
paragraphs: You tell yourself you will search only one thing.
A message sent three years ago to someone called Maya:

03c.title: THE SEARCH
paragraphs: This one contains a lawyer’s letter.
The $47,263 came originally from an inheritance.
Your spouse’s mother left the money with an unusual instruction:
“Keep this separate. One day you may need the freedom to leave.”

03d.title: SILENCE
paragraphs: You look at the person you have shared eleven years with.
Except now there is $47,263 sitting invisibly in the room.
“There was nothing useful in there,” you say.

04.title: DINNER
paragraphs: Dinner is almost finished when your spouse says:
“I’ve been thinking. Maybe we should postpone the holiday. Money is a bit tight.”

05d.title: ANOTHER NIGHT
paragraphs: The next morning your spouse leaves for work.
Can we talk tonight? There is something I should have told you years ago.
Perhaps your spouse knows you found the statement.

05.title: THE EXPLANATION
paragraphs: Your spouse takes a long time before speaking.
“Mum worked in London on overseas contracts paid in US dollars. I kept the inheritance in a dollar account here.”
“She left me some money. She didn’t trust you with it.”
Years ago, there was a period when you were taking financial risks.
Before she died, she created an emergency fund for her child.
Money that could never be touched by the marriage.

06.title: THE PROBLEM
paragraphs: Your spouse answers the last question whether you asked it or not.
You look at the statement again.
“Then where did the rest come from?”
This wasn’t simply an inheritance kept separate.
For years, while the two of you discussed bills, school fees, repairs, holidays and savings…
your spouse was quietly moving money somewhere else.

07.title: MAYA
paragraphs: You have never heard the name before.
A sister your spouse almost never discusses.
Maya is joint holder of the account.
If anything happened, she could access the money.

08a.title: THE CALL
paragraphs: Your spouse puts the phone on speaker.
“I wondered when this day would come.”
“Before you get angry with me, there’s something you should know.”

08b.title: KEEP OUT
paragraphs: “I don’t want your sister in our marriage.”
“When things were bad, Maya was the person I talked to.”
“You talked to everybody about the investment.”
“I needed one person who was mine.”
That sentence lands harder than expected.

08c.title: WHAT MAYA KNOWS
paragraphs: The year neither of you discusses anymore.

08d.title: OUTSIDE
paragraphs: Walk without deciding where you are going.
Before you decide what this means, remember what happened eleven years ago.

09.title: ELEVEN YEARS AGO
paragraphs: Especially the argument in which they were wrong.
Shortly after the wedding, you invested heavily in a business opportunity.
You used some joint savings anyway.
You promised you would replace them.
At least you thought it did.
“You remember it as an investment that worked out.”
“I remember it as the day I realised you could make a decision with our money without me.”
Because your spouse has spent years doing something remarkably similar.

12a.title: WHY
paragraphs: “I’m not saying that makes what I did right.”
There is an uncomfortable difference between an excuse and an explanation.
You are no longer certain which one you have just heard.

12d.title: THE ANSWER
paragraphs: “Nothing. I would have respected your decision.”
Because neither of you can prove what the person you were years ago would have done.

end-a.title: STAY
paragraphs: You stay. Your spouse finishes the deposit history; you explain the joint savings you once invested. Neither of you promises that staying tonight has settled it.

You set a time tomorrow and list the bills that cannot wait. Your spouse brings their contribution record; you agree to bring your own. No money moves tonight, and the question about the old joint savings is still on the page.
Your spouse brings the statement to tomorrow’s discussion themselves. No copy has been sent outside the home.
At breakfast you use two mugs and one notebook. The dishes from last night are still waiting. Nobody volunteers the statement for washing-up duty.

end-b.title: DISCLOSURE
paragraphs: You agree to exchange account and debt records from both of you. Your spouse supplies current statements; you supply your outstanding loan schedule. Neither person gains authority to operate the other’s account.

Your loan repayments leave less for the joint budget than your spouse expected. You postpone the appliance repair together and agree a Friday contribution schedule based on both sets of figures, without closing the separate account.
Your spouse brings the statement to tomorrow’s discussion themselves. No copy has been sent outside the home.
The next envelope on the table is addressed to both of you. It contains the bills for the meeting, not an answer about the marriage.

end-c.title: LEAVE
paragraphs: You leave for the night and say you will decide tomorrow. Your spouse asks for a time to resume. You send one after reaching your cousin’s house, rather than leave them waiting for a return you have not promised.
Your cousin’s sofa is shorter than you remembered. You miss the early journey you usually share and pay your own taxi fare. The bill discussion waits for the time you sent.
Your spouse brings the statement to tomorrow’s discussion themselves. No copy has been sent outside the home.
Tomorrow has a place and a time. Tonight has a borrowed blanket and a phone you decide to leave face down.

end-d.title: YOUR SECRET
paragraphs: You stay silent about your next plan. Tomorrow you open a separate account without telling your spouse.
You pay the opening charges from your own funds and keep the new account out of the household notebook. Friday’s figures no longer match the contribution your spouse was expecting.
Your spouse brings the statement to tomorrow’s discussion themselves. No copy has been sent outside the home.
The next bill arrives before either bank statement. Your spouse asks how much you can send. You have a new account and the same kitchen table.
